name: Gulgula
ingredients: Mustard oil or Ghee for deep frying
instructions: 1. Dissolve the jaggery in warm water and strain it to remove impurities. 2. In a bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, fennel seeds, cardamom powder, and a pinch of salt. 3. Gradually add the jaggery water to the flour mixture to form a smooth, thick, and lump-free batter. 4. Let the batter rest for at least 30 minutes to allow the flour to hydrate. 5. Heat oil or ghee in a deep pan over medium heat. 6. Carefully drop small spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil. 7. Fry until the Gulgulas turn golden brown and crisp on the outside, ensuring they are cooked through. 8. Drain on paper towels and serve warm or at room temperature.
description: Gulgula is a quintessential comfort food in the Pahari culture of Uttarakhand. These sweet, bite-sized fritters are often prepared during festivals, religious ceremonies, or as an anytime snack. They hold a nostalgic place in local households, symbolizing simple, wholesome sweetness, and are a staple offering in traditional mountain hospitality.
